findings.text: follow-on: FINDING_CLAIM_FIELDS duplicates review.FINDING_CLAIM_FIELDS (reckon/crew/review.py:156), the owner of that capability, rather than importing it; the parity test keeps the copy in step so it does not hold the node, but a second declaration of an owned constant is a divergence that only a test prevents.

follow-on: _unreadable_record_remedy tells the two faults apart by matching the reader's human-readable error prose (_CLAIMLESS_RECORD_ERROR at :117) instead of a structured fault code, so any rewording of review.py:2828's ValueError silently reverts the duty to the mid-write remedy; only the end-to-end test test_a_claimless_record_names_its_fault_and_does_not_wait catches that, the direct unit test carrying the same literal.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit f23bd6de8 against 204afb91dc; three files changed — obligation_snapshot.py splitting the remedy on the reader's reported error and removing the dead watch_reload_started_at wrapper, a new 264-line test file, and a 21-line evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_an_unreadable_review_duty_names_its_fault.py; the manifest records the new file 5 passed EXIT=0 and the base/head arms over the importing files (head 103/0, base 98/0), which I re-ran (5 passed at head), and its ruff arm, unrecorded in the manifest, I re-ran as "All checks passed" and "2 files already formatted".
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to make the unreadable review record duty tell a claimless complete record from one caught mid-write; reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:584 _unreadable_record_remedy now returns the claimless remedy when the reader's error names claimless findings and today's mid-write remedy otherwise, wired at :630.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete; it records commit f23bd6de842b8771fcc8031b804b537ae5cb23e8, base 98 passed/0 failed and head 103 passed/0 failed over two chunks each, and a negative control at 3 failed EXIT=1.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the source manifest declares reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py, tests/test_an_unreadable_review_duty_names_its_fault.py, the evidence fragment and a figure dir; the diff's three changed paths all sit inside that set and no figure was written.

justifications.durability: negative-control-claimless-remedy-restored.log shows the single mid-write remedy reddening test_a_claimless_record_names_its_fault_and_does_not_wait and test_the_remedy_tells_the_two_faults_apart at EXIT=1, and test_the_claim_fields_mirror_the_review_reader compares two independent module constants.
justifications.evidence: the done_when's pytest cases are asserted in tests/test_an_unreadable_review_duty_names_its_fault.py and recorded in the manifest and gate logs, but the manifest records no ruff result even though the done_when names ruff check and format as part of the gate.
justifications.fit: _unreadable_record_remedy and _CLAIMLESS_RECORD_ERROR follow the module's existing private-helper idiom at reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:570 and carry no plan, ticket or version label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:584-603 returns the claimless remedy for the reader's claimless error string and the mid-write remedy otherwise, which is exactly the section's deliverable.
justifications.reuse: FINDING_CLAIM_FIELDS at reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:126 re-declares review.py:156's tuple rather than importing it, mitigated by the parity test at tests/test_an_unreadable_review_duty_names_its_fault.py:260.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path (reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py, tests/test_an_unreadable_review_duty_names_its_fault.py, docs/evidence/fragments/every-review-is-kept-as-a-committed-record/an-unreadable-review-duty-names-its-fault.html) is inside the source manifest's declared write paths.
